items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: And then, I remember the Turks were here. They were people that were dog-skinned, reddish complexion, with jet black string hair, beautiful.

ctx.x: Well, as they say, New Orleans was a melting pot and that's a good name to give it. Because in my wife's family, they're Filipinos, they're Chinamans, and they're various other races. And then, I remember the Turks were here. They were people that were dog-skinned, reddish complexion, with jet black string hair, beautiful. And they're intermarried and if you notice around New Orleans, they can find a lot of these fellow clown hair. But that type of hair, that complexion, they call them a nickname, Turk. Well,…

Well, you know, at one time they had a lot of Turkish tunes out, you know, American songs, but with Turkish tones, flavor to them. That's right. And Chinese flavor and all that. And I wondered why. People here liked them. Maybe that had something to do with it?
